I was told not to come here... but what I found was unlike anywhere else on Earth.

Hidden on the outskirts of Karachi lies the Manghopir Shrine, one of Pakistan's oldest and most mysterious Sufi shrines. For centuries, pilgrims have travelled here seeking blessings, bathing in its natural sulphur hot springs, and visiting the shrine of the revered saint Pir Mangho. But what makes this place truly extraordinary is something almost impossible to believe until you see it for yourself: more than 200 sacred crocodiles living inside the shrine complex.

This wasn't always a place visitors felt safe exploring. Around a decade ago, the surrounding area became a Taliban stronghold, forcing security forces into a years-long operation to reclaim it. Even today, locals still warn outsiders about visiting, and security raids have continued in the area in recent years.

In this video, I travel into Manghopir to uncove
title: I Was Warned Not to Visit This Shrine in Taliban Territory
